name: Smartphones

comps.spec: GPS receiver that works with no SIM, signal or internet once offline maps are loaded
comps.loc: The whole phone: keep it working

comps.spec: FM broadcast radio on many budget Android phones — wired earphones act as the antenna; needs no network
comps.loc: Built in; look for an FM radio app

comps.spec: Single 3.7–3.85V lithium pouch, 2,000–5,000 mAh — glued in; never pry with metal, bend or puncture it
comps.loc: Under the back cover or the screen

comps.spec: Camera modules, 8–50 MP, with an LED flash that doubles as a torch
OLED or LCD touchscreen, 5–7 in — glued in and cracks easily
Vibration motor (coin or linear type), about 3V
Tiny neodymium magnets in the speakers, vibration motor and (some models) a charging ring
Surface-mount Hall sensor that detects flip covers (many models)

boards.loc: Small protection board on the battery

notes: A working phone beats its parts: with offline maps and files it is a GPS, camera, torch, library and voice recorder that charges from any 5V USB source. Drawers of dead phones still hold lithium cells and magnets; check each cell for swelling before charging.

sources.title: Weight: smartphones averaged 0.14 kg (Babbitt et al. 2020, disassembly-based bill of materials data for consumer electronics, CC0)
Open Repair Alliance, Open Repair Data v0.3 (community repair events, 2012 to July 2026; CC BY-SA 4.0): 6,290 repairs recorded as Mobile
